faqs.q: Can I claim a tax deduction for my child's ICSE school fees?
faqs.a: Yes, but only the tuition fee part and only under the old tax regime. Tuition fees for up to two children count towards the overall limit of ₹1.5 lakh a year, which moved from Section 80C to Section 123 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 from April 2026. Admission, transport, development and activity fees do not qualify, and the new tax regime gives no such deduction.

faqs.q: What is the difference between ICSE and CBSE schools?
faqs.a: ICSE schools follow the syllabus of the Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations, which is known for its detailed coverage and strong focus on English and languages. CBSE schools follow the Central Board of Secondary Education, whose NCERT-based syllabus is closely aligned with national entrance exams such as JEE and NEET. Neither is better for every child.

faqs.q: Are ICSE schools more expensive than CBSE schools in Pune?
faqs.a: Often, yes. ICSE schools in Pune generally charge more than CBSE and state board schools, mostly because of their infrastructure, smaller classes and extra activities. Fees still vary widely from school to school within each board, so compare the full fee structure of the schools you are considering rather than going by the board alone.

faqs.q: What should parents ask a school about fees before admission?
faqs.a: Ask for the full fee structure in writing, including tuition, admission, development, transport, books, uniform and activity charges. Check how much fees usually rise each year, whether you can pay in instalments, whether sibling discounts apply, and what the refund rules are if your child leaves the school mid-year.
